Q1: To start, please tell me your current seniority and function. As an example, you might say something like: "I'm a senior manager in finance."
Q2: How many years have you worked in your current company?
Q3: Thanks. What industry is your company in? And, roughly, how many people work at your company?
Q4: Currently, does your team use one platform or several different tools for HR, payroll, and benefits? What is the main software or set of tools that you use?
Q5: Got it. I'd like you to think back to the last time your team considered buying an HR, payroll, or benefits tool. How long ago was that?
Q6: Back then, what software or tools were you using when you started this evaluation?
Q7: Back then, what motivated your team to consider other HR, payroll, or benefits tools? Please share all of the factors that motivated you.
Q8: Was there anything else happening more broadly at your company or industry that motivated you to consider other tools?
Q9: Thanks. At that time, was your HR, payroll, or benefits tools causing any particular frustrations or challenges that you were hoping another tool might solve?
Q10: Which tools did you seriously consider? Please list the names of the tools you considered.
Q11: Did you have any minimum criteria that a tool had to have in order to be seriously considered? If so, what was your criteria?
Q12: Who else, if anyone, was involved in the final decision during this evaluation? What role did they play?
Q13: After your evaluation, did you purchase and switch to a new one or just continue using your previous software or tools? And if you purchased one, which one?
Q14: Why did you choose that tool (the one you switched to or stayed with)? How did it stand out and why did you prefer it to the others?
Q15: For each of the tools that you considered, but rejected, please share the main reasons why each tool was not chosen.
Q16: Now, I want to switch and talk about the present and what it's like working with your current HR, payroll, and benefits software or tools. What does your current tool(s) do well?
Q17: Where does it fall short of what you need today?
Q18: What is your biggest frustration with your current tool(s)? Please describe it and the level of frustration it causes you or your team.
Q19: What, if anything, has changed about your needs since the last time you considered HR, payroll, and benefits tools?
Q20: On an annual basis, how much, roughly, do you think your company spends on your current HR, payroll, and benefits tool(s)?
Q21: Do you think the cost is reasonable relative to the value your company gets?
Q22: Now, please think back to the biggest frustration with your current HR, payroll, and benefits tool(s) that you shared earlier. Imagine that a feature could be added to your current solution that would solve that frustration. How much do you think that would be worth to your company on an annual basis?
Q23: Within the next 6 months, do you think you'll likely consider switching to any new HR, payroll, and benefits tools? If so, if you had to guess, how likely do you think you'll switch from your current tool or tools?
Q24: Lastly, looking at a broader level, what do you think most people in your position would say are the biggest challenges with HR, payroll, and benefits tool(s) today?
